capabilities.summary: Keyframes written at times and named beats are compile-time lowerings onto ordinary track start, duration and offsets.
restrictions: MotionScript only: Scene IR is unchanged, no requires token is added and the emitter writes the percentage form. Wire stays 0.2; MotionScript 0.1 programs reject beats and timed keys.

keyframes accepts `at <time> <value> [ease …] [spatial …];`. The track starts at the first key and lasts until the last; offsets are exact quotients (secondsKeysToTrack). Keys strictly increase, at least two are required, and start / duration headers are rejected with timed keys. Mixing percentage and timed keys in one track is rejected. Times are in the track's own domain (scope-local under timing).

`beat <name> at <time | beat ± time>;` is a compile-time constant time. A reference names an earlier beat only (forward references are rejected even when the unit waits for a node), names are unique, and results are finite and >= 0. Beats add nothing to Scene IR, may follow a seal, and cannot appear inside a batch. `beat` matches by spelling and is not a reserved word.

Time positions that may name a beat: animate / keyframes start, timed key at, step at, seal, timing offset and cue at. Lengths (duration, cue offset/duration/fades) do not take a beat. Beats do not create scopes; a beat-local track uses an affine timing scope whose offset is the beat.

Gaps between per-beat tracks follow the pinned E014 rule: the later track owns a shared boundary, the latest-ended fill forwards writer holds in a gap, otherwise the authored base applies, and there is no backwards fill.

capabilities.summary: A timing scope may wrap its local time with a period, optionally a finite repeat count; steps may follow a cyclic scope.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing timing.cyclicScopes; the compiler adds it when a timing declares a period. periodMs / repeat / step timingScopeId without the capability are rejected. Scopes without a period map exactly as timing.localScopes.

MotionScript `timing <id> { period <duration>; repeat <n>; }`. period is a positive length (no beat); repeat is an integer in 1..10000 and requires a period. period and repeat match by spelling inside timing and are not reserved words.

Unbounded cycle: local = wrap((parent - offset) / stretch, period), non-negative on both sides of the offset, so the offset is a phase. Cycles are half-open: local is never the period itself. Finite repeat: negative (not entered) before affine time 0, wraps for N periods, then pinned at the period. Anything below an unentered finite repeat is not entered either. Nesting under or over affine scopes applies root to leaf (cyclicLocalTimeMs). Expressions see local_t and progress from the cyclic local time; t stays absolute.

A track or step in a cyclic chain lies inside one period of its innermost cycle, measured through affine scopes below it. Steps may name a scope only when its chain has a period. At local time L the step value is the last step at or before L; before a cycle's first step the previous cycle's final step carries over, except before the first cycle of a finite repeat.

Exclusive ownership: a channel written inside a cyclic chain is owned by that chain. Root, affine-scoped, other-cycle tracks and root steps on the same scalar are OVERLAPPING_WRITERS. Writers in the same cycle are compared in that cycle's local frame.

Streaming: a writer may join a cyclic chain only while the sealed frontier has not passed the chain's entry (cyclicWriterAdmissible). Unbounded cycles, and cycles under negative stretch, have entry -Infinity: all their writers must arrive before the first seal. The compiler reports INVALID_TIMING, the stream linter SEALED_HISTORY_WRITE, and delta admission rejects the delta.

Out of scope: composition-instance timing (forbidden since Scene IR 0.25.0 / MotionScript 0.26.0), loops, functions, timers, a scene-level loop flag (host playback), periods that change over time, shortest-arc rotation and velocity-facing. Lottie and SVG are not imported.

capabilities.summary: An image resource may be an atlas grid; an image node draws one row-major cell named by an integer frame, which may be animated.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing resources.spriteFrames; the compiler adds it when an image declares frames. ImageResource.frames, ImageNode.frame and frame tracks without the capability are MISSING_REQUIRED.

MotionScript `frames (columns, rows);` lowers onto the node's image resource as { columns, rows } (whole numbers 1..1024). `frame <n>;` is a static row-major index 0 <= n < columns x rows and needs frames. frames and frame match by spelling and are not reserved words; they apply only to image nodes.

The `frame` node channel is a number track (animate / keyframes / timed keys, local and cyclic scopes) on an image whose resource has a grid. Sampled values are floored (with a 1e-9 tolerance), then clamped to [0, count - 1]; non-finite values show frame 0. So `from 0; to N; duration D` shows N frames for D/N each and holds the last. Seals and late writers follow the ordinary track rules.

Renderer: the cell rectangle is derived from the decoded image size (width / columns, height / rows), so programs never state source pixels; the cell is drawn at the node size. Uneven atlas sizes give fractional source rects. Per-cell sizes, padding, trimmed atlases, frame-rate sugar and pattern paint are out of scope.

capabilities.summary: Planar 2.5D layers opt into seam/split compositing: true surface intersections are split along their plane intersection into ordered fragments, and declared seams are checked for a shared edge in view space.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. A spatial layer's seams object requires space.planarSeams (and space.planar25d) in requiredCapabilities / requires; without it the scene is rejected. Layers without seams keep the 0.12.0 report-only behaviour exactly.

seams: split (boolean, default true), edgeEpsilon (> 0, default 0.001 logical units), maxFragments (integer 0..1024, default 64 extra draw items per layer per frame), edges (pairs of distinct surfaces of the same layer, no duplicates).

Plane tests stay the occlusion authority. A pair whose outlines straddle each other's planes is clipped along the exact plane-plane line in item space; fragments keep node id, appearance and paint slot and are ordered by the same plane tests. Fragment paint outlines overlap the cut by 0.5 logical px to avoid anti-aliased hairlines. Text, image, open-outline and stroked surfaces are not split (SPATIAL_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED) and over-budget pairs are left unsplit (SPATIAL_SPLIT_LIMIT); both keep SPATIAL_SURFACES_INTERSECT.

Declared seam edges report SPATIAL_SEAM_OPEN when the two projected outlines share no collinear overlapping edge within edgeEpsilon; geometric coincidence is required, not visual similarity. Shared edges never suppress an intersection. Order hints are a host option (projectSpatialFrame orderHint), applied to ties only; no authored or animated order channel is in this release.

capabilities.summary: A node attaches to a path node at a progress in [0, 1] along its resolved (morphed, then trimmed) outline, optionally oriented to the tangent and optionally rolling.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing geometry.pathProgress; pathAttachments without it are rejected.

MotionScript `attach <node> along <path> { progress n; orient b; rollRadius r; }` lowers to Scene IR pathAttachments (base definitions on CREATE_SCENE, frozen after the first seal). progress is required and in [0, 1]; the path must be a path node in the root scene; a node has at most one attachment. attach and along are the only reserved words.

Sampling resolves the path commands after path morph (geometry.pathMorph) and then the same trim rules frame resolution uses (geometry.operators / geometry.animatedTrim), so late morph or trim changes move the node without re-baking progress. Progress is the base value unless a path.progress track on the attached node supplies it.

Without geometry.pathSpace, the sampled position is the path's local command space written directly to transform.position; place the node and the path in the same parent space with a neutral path transform. Distance and arc length use the 8-sample-per-curve table shared with geometry.trimPath, measured over the trimmed outline.

An attachment exclusively owns transform.position.x/y on its node. When orient is true or rollRadius is set it also owns transform.rotation, written as (orient ? tangent angle : 0) + (rollRadius ? distance / rollRadius : 0). orient alone is never rolling. Timeline tracks, interact bindings and physics writes on owned channels are rejected as OVERLAPPING_WRITERS. path.progress tracks (number in [0, 1]) are legal only on attached nodes.

Markers, arrowhead styling, stroke dash (paint.strokeDash), width profiles and transform.autoOrient as a standalone channel are outside this claim. Composed path transforms are geometry.pathSpace. Lottie ks.ao and SVG path progress are not imported.

capabilities.summary: A path attachment places its traveller on the path as drawn: the command point is mapped through the path node's sampled transform into the traveller's parent space.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing geometry.pathSpace together with geometry.pathProgress. The compiler adds both when it lowers attach. No new syntax or reserved words.

Sampling maps the command point by inverse(traveller parent world) × path world, using the sampled local matrix (position, pivot, rotation, scale) and transformParentId when set, otherwise parentId. The camera is not part of that matrix. Rotation, when orient or rollRadius is set, uses the transformed tangent plus command-space distance/radius. rollRadius does not follow visual scale.
Scenes that require geometry.pathProgress and not geometry.pathSpace keep the 0.17 path-local write. Identity path transforms with a shared transform parent match that write.

The traveller and the path must resolve to the same root space (both world or both screen). A mismatch is SPACE_VIOLATION and the attachment is not applied. A singular parent transform or a degenerate oriented tangent is RUNTIME_DEGRADED and leaves the authored pose or rolling-only rotation. Attachment cycles are CYCLE and those poses stay authored.

The value written is transform.position, not a pivot-compensated local origin. A non-zero traveller pivot offsets the drawn origin the same way it does for any other node. Lottie and SVG are not imported.

capabilities.summary: A group render scope keeps descendant pixels only where another node's painted alpha is.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing compositing.matte.
Group compositing.matte.nodeId names any node outside that group: not itself, an ancestor, or a descendant. Matte cycles are rejected.

The source may be hidden with visible false and is still sampled. A visible source also paints in order. Alpha is the painted result of that node and its subtree, including opacity, text, images, gradients and existing blur.
The renderer composites with a content buffer and a coverage buffer per matted scope (destination-in) and withholds the scope when a buffer cannot be allocated.

capabilities.summary: A group render scope clips its descendants to another node's outline.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing compositing.mask.
Group compositing.clip.geometryId names a rectangle, circle, ellipse, polygon or path in the same scene. Text, image, line and group targets are rejected.

Clip implies an isolated render scope. The clip outline uses the target node's viewport logicalMatrix; nested clips intersect. Dedicated clip shapes typically set visible false; a visible source still paints.

Hit-testing requires the pointer to lie inside every ancestor clip. Alpha track mattes are compositing.matte. Luma masks, feathering and inverted clips are outside both claims. Lottie masksProperties and SVG clipPath stay unsupported / untested.

capabilities.summary: Discrete content updates and numeric format bindings on text.basic nodes; display strings derive from formatNumber / resolveNumericContent.
restrictions: Wire stays 0.2. Scenes and programs gate with requiredCapabilities / requires containing text.dynamicContent; text numeric bindings, content steps and text.number tracks without it are rejected.
MotionScript text body fields number / fractionDigits / minIntegerDigits / sign / group / decimal / prefix / suffix lower to TextNode.numeric. Format fields require number. No new reserved words.
animate Node.number writes the text.number channel and is legal only on a text node with a numeric binding. Sampling sets content via resolveNumericContent(sampledNumber, format).

step Node.content { at t; value "…"; } writes discrete single-line string content. Continuous string interpolation is not offered. Content steps require a text node and cannot share a node with a numeric binding (OVERLAPPING_WRITERS).
Layout metrics / font readiness (text.layoutMetrics), per-glyph animators (text.animators), wrapping / multi-line and Lottie text-animator import are outside this claim.
